scenarios.title: halo rev A rail: CR2032 at 3.0 V / 30 ohm, 40 uF bulk, nRF54L10 3.7 mA TX pulse
scenarios.why: nominal 3.0 V (Energizer Form 2032NA0618, Specifications) with the only pulse impedance derivable from stated numbers, 30.3 ohm

constants.name: i_tx_A
constants.source: nRF54L10 datasheet (Nordic 4503_018 v0.10) Table 86, ITX,0dBm = 3.7 mA, radio-only TX current at 0 dBm. Transcribed in ce-designs/halo/research/fetched/E-nrf54l-datasheet-currents.md. NOT the 4.8 mA on Nordic's product page, which is a whole-device figure.

constants.name: i_sleep_A
constants.source: Table 86, ION_IDLE4 = 2.4 uA, System ON with 192 kB of RAM retained, which is the nRF54L10's whole RAM. research/05 §11.2 notes Nordic publishes no 192 kB + GRTC + LFXO row, so the advertising sleep state is bracketed by 2.0 and 3.1 uA and this uses the retention figure alone.

constants.name: bulk_F
constants.source: 4 x 10 uF 0402 X5R 6.3V (C9-C12). NOT Apple's five 100 uF: D12 deleted the U1 and D11a deleted the class-D amplifier, which were two of the three loads that needed 500 uF, and an 0805 is 1.25 mm tall against a 0.578 mm bottom-face allowance.

constants.name: capacity_mAh
constants.source: Energizer CR2032 Form No. 2032NA0618, Specifications: 'Typical Capacity 235 mAh (to 2.0 volts), Rated at 15K ohms at 21C'

constants.name: nrf54l_vdd_min_V
constants.source: nRF54L operating supply range low limit, 1.7 V

constants.name: floor_V
constants.source: the assert floor: nrf54l_vdd_min_V plus 100 mV of margin

constants.name: ocv_V
constants.source: Energizer Form 2032NA0618 Specifications / TI SWRA349's stated end-of-life threshold — see the point's own why

constants.name: esr_ohm
constants.source: nominal 3.0 V (Energizer Form 2032NA0618, Specifications) with the only pulse impedance derivable from stated numbers, 30.3 ohm

measurements.name: v_rest_V
measurements.why: the rail at rest, one ms before the transmission starts

measurements.name: v_min_V
measurements.why: the deepest point of the droop, at the end of the 1 ms transmit slot

measurements.name: droop_mV
measurements.why: how far the rail falls during one transmission

measurements.name: i_peak_mA
measurements.why: peak current the CELL delivers. The bulk supplies the rest of the 3.7 mA, which is what it is for

measurements.name: i_avg_uA
measurements.why: time-weighted average cell current over one full 2 s period; battery life divides into this

measurements.name: life_months
measurements.why: capacity_mAh / average mA / 730.5 h per month. IDEAL: it spends every stated mAh and models no self-discharge, no temperature and no capacity lost to pulsing

measurements.name: life_months_derated
measurements.why: the same figure with the two derations that can be cited: TI SWRA349 Figure 3, 9 % average capacity loss for pulsed draw, and Energizer's ~1 %/year self-discharge

asserts.name: v_min_V
asserts.why: below 1.8 V there is under 100 mV to the nRF54L's 1.7 V minimum; the radio browns out mid-transmission and the tag goes silent

asserts.name: droop_mV
asserts.why: a droop this side of 400 mV means the 40 uF bulk, and not the cell, is carrying the transmission — which is the design intent (TI SWRA349 section 4)

asserts.name: i_peak_mA
asserts.why: the cell must never see the full 3.7 mA edge; if it does, the bulk is too small and every pulse is drawn through the ESR

scenarios.title: halo rev A: the cell is REMOVED at t = 0.5 s and the 40 uF bulk holds the rail up
scenarios.why: SPEC.md §3: the bulk capacitance is 'what keeps the tag alive for seconds after the cell is pulled, which is how the five-removals reset works'. Apple has 500 uF for it; rev A has 40 uF and this measures what that buys.

measurements.name: v_before_V
measurements.why: the rail with the cell still in

measurements.name: v_at_1s_V
measurements.why: one second after the cell leaves

measurements.name: v_at_10s_V
measurements.why: ten seconds after the cell leaves

measurements.name: v_at_30s_V
measurements.why: thirty seconds after — the end of the run

measurements.name: holdup_to_1v7_s
measurements.why: how long the rail stays above the nRF54L's 1.7 V minimum after the cell leaves, at sleep current. t = C dV / I, exact for a constant-current discharge.

measurements.name: holdup_apple_500uF_s
measurements.why: the same figure with Apple's five 100 uF instead of our four 10 uF — the cost of D-4's re-sizing, as a number

asserts.name: holdup_to_1v7_s
asserts.why: the firmware must detect the removal, count it and commit the count before the rail dies. That budget is about 11 ms (0.24 ms sense collapse + <1 ms sample + <=10 ms NVM write) and 100 ms is it with 10x margin. THE NVM WRITE TIME IS NOT SOURCED - Nordic's RRAM write figure was not fetched - so the 10 ms is a bounded estimate and this assert is only as good as that bound.

asserts.name: v_at_1s_V
asserts.why: a full second of life after the cell leaves, which is roughly a hundred times the detect-and-commit budget
